stem:
Alok draws two rays from a common point $P$ on his notebook: ray $PM$ and ray $PN$.

One or more options may be correct. Which two claims correctly describe the angle they form?

options.text: Ray $PM$ and ray $PN$ form an angle whose vertex is $P$ and whose arms are $PM$ and $PN$.
The vertex of the angle is arm $PM$.
The angle may be named $\angle MPN$, with the vertex letter $P$ written in the middle.
Ray $PM$ and another ray that does not start at $P$ still form this angle.

teacher.key_rationale: Two rays from P form an angle with vertex P and arms PM, PN; the three-letter name puts P in the middle. Calling an arm the vertex swaps terms. Dropping the shared starting point omits the angle condition.
